CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 17th September, 2014 passed in MVC No.3119/2012 on the file of the II Additional Small Causes Judge & XXVIII ACMM, Bengaluru, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity), seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text:
2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for respondent No.1 - insurance company and perused the material on record.
3.
The occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained by the claimant and coverage of insurance are not in dispute.

For having sustained injuries due to the accident, the Tribunal has granted compensation under various heads as follows:
NC: 2024:KHC:45731 i) Injury, pain & sufferings Rs.50,000-00 ii) Loss of leave encashment benefit Rs.49,155-00 iii) Loss of amenities Rs.10,000-00 iv) Conveyance, Nourishment, food and attendant charges Rs.16,000-00 ..............................

sentences.text:
In the present case, from the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant had suffered the following injuries:
a) Anterior dislocation of left hip b) Left pubic rami fracture and pubic symphysis fracture c) Abrasion over left hand and left knee 5.
The claimant was aged 59 years old as on the date of accident.
He was working as Manager in the Central Jail, Bengaluru.

Though the claimant suffered grievous injuries, he was not terminated from service and he was allowed to continue in the same job by drawing the same salary and retired on attaining the age of superannuation.
Therefore, question of granting compensation under the head of loss of income due to disability, would not arise.
Further, it is submitted that the claimant has got reimbursement of medical expenses and hospital charges.
But the compensation awarded towards injury, pain & sufferings; loss of amenities; and conveyance, nourishment, food and attendant charges, are on the lower side.

Therefore considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant, if another sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded in global in addition to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, is just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.

7. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 17th September 2014 passed in MVC No.3119/2012, on the file of II Additional Small Causes Judge & XXVIII ACMM,
Bengaluru, stands modified to an extent that the appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional global compensation of Rs.25,000/-
(Rupees twenty-five thousand only), along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
